finding.claim: A negative integer in a Relay 'before' cursor sets end to a negative value, bypassing the 'first' clamp and the relay_max_results cap, so a sequence-backed connection returns all but the last few items in one request.
finding.source: Client-supplied 'before' argument: base64 of 'arrayconnection:-5' (prefix check at utils.py:146-148 passes).
finding.sink: strawberry/relay/types.py:887-890 sequence slice nodes[start:overfetch], where overfetch = end+1 (utils.py:109-111).

trace.note: Cursor decoded; prefix validated against PREFIX.
With first=10, end = min(-5, 0+10) = -5, so the first clamp is ineffective.
expected = end - start = -5; end is not None, so the max_results default is skipped.
nodes[0:-4] returns all but the last four elements.
Overfetch check len==expected+1 never matches; has_next_page false.

finding.guards_checked: Cursor prefix check (passes with a valid prefix); first/last non-negative and <= max_results checks (only when the argument is present, and not applied to the derived end); relay_max_results not enforced on this path; per-node resolve_node still runs so field permissions apply. Non-sequence iterables use islice (types.py:893-897), which rejects negative values, and Django querysets reject negative slicing, so those error instead of bypassing. Impact is unbounded page size, not access to items the connection would not serve across pages.

finding.claim: _entities builds federation entities from every field in the client's representation (no resolve_reference), so non-key fields such as owner_id are attacker-chosen and can satisfy permission checks that read source fields.
finding.source: Public _entities query 'representations' argument: {__typename, id, <any GraphQL field of the type>}.
finding.sink: Field-level permission checks and resolvers that read the source object's fields (e.g. owner_id, id) to authorize or load protected data.

trace.note: __typename popped from representation; type resolved from type_map.
No resolve_reference on type, so convert_argument is called on the whole representation.
Loops over all type fields and copies every field present in the input into kwargs.
type_(**kwargs) instantiates the entity with attacker-chosen values; no DB fetch and no key-only filter.
Field copies preserve PermissionExtension, so permission checks still run against the fabricated source object.

finding.guards_checked: Field-level PermissionExtension still runs and is not bypassed (types/field.py:178-201 copies extensions). _entities itself has no permission and nothing enforces that representations contain only @key fields. Exploitability depends on application code: a @key type with no resolve_reference, a permission or resolver reading non-key fields, and a publicly reachable subgraph endpoint.
